plan: In a second-price auction, the optimal strategy is to bid exactly my true value, since I pay the second-highest bid if I win, not my own bid. Bidding my value ensures I win whenever profitable (value exceeds others' bids) and never overpay. With a low value of $4, I should bid $4 to reflect this straightforward dominant strategy, ensuring maximum expected profit given the uniform distribution of competitors' values.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy: you pay the second-highest bid if you win, so shading your bid only risks losing profitable auctions without reducing what you pay. With no information suggesting otherwise, and this being a one-shot game, I'll bid exactly my value of $23 to maximize expected profit.

In a second-price (Vickrey) auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds the second-highest bid, and you pay that second-highest bid regardless of your own bid (as long as you're still the highest). Overbidding risks paying more than your value if you win; underbidding risks losing profitable auctions. Since this is a one-shot game with no repeated learning needed, I will bid exactly my true value of $32 to maximize expected profit.
